## [Comprehensive Rust — Naming Conventions](comprehensive-rust-naming-conventions.md)

| ID | Title | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [CR-NAM-01](comprehensive-rust-naming-conventions.md#cr-nam-01) | `new`: constructor functions | `new` (as a whole method name or as a prefix) **SHOULD** name the "default" constructor function for a type. |
| [CR-NAM-02](comprehensive-rust-naming-conventions.md#cr-nam-02) | `is_[condition]`: boolean check | A method that checks a boolean condition about a value **SHOULD** be named `is_[condition]`; **SHOULD NOT** put `not` in the name (no `is_not_` methods) — callers write `!value.is_[condition]()` instead. |
| [CR-NAM-03](comprehensive-rust-naming-conventions.md#cr-nam-03) | `[method]_mut`: mutable reference access | An access-style method that gives access to a mutable reference **SHOULD** use the `_mut` suffix, paired with an immutable version that gets the shorter name. |
| [CR-NAM-04](comprehensive-rust-naming-conventions.md#cr-nam-04) | `with` as constructor | A constructor that sets one value of a type while using default values for the rest **MAY** use the `with_` prefix, read as "`<Type>` with specific setting". |
| [CR-NAM-05](comprehensive-rust-naming-conventions.md#cr-nam-05) | `with` as copy-and-set | A method that copies a value but changes a specific part of it **MAY** use the `with_` prefix, read as "like `<value>`, but with something different". |
| [CR-NAM-06](comprehensive-rust-naming-conventions.md#cr-nam-06) | `with`: working with closures | A method that takes a function or closure to use instead of a "sensible default" computation **MAY** use the `_with` suffix, read as "do X, but with this specific way of computing things". |
| [CR-NAM-07](comprehensive-rust-naming-conventions.md#cr-nam-07) | `try_[method]`: fallible methods with specific errors | A method that can fail and returns a `Result` **SHOULD** use the `try_` prefix. |
| [CR-NAM-08](comprehensive-rust-naming-conventions.md#cr-nam-08) | `from`: conversion constructors | The `from_` prefix **SHOULD** be used for constructor-style, `From`-trait-style functions that strongly imply a type conversion; `new` **SHOULD** still be preferred for most constructor-style functions. |
| [CR-NAM-09](comprehensive-rust-naming-conventions.md#cr-nam-09) | `into`: consuming conversion | A method that consumes `self` and returns an owned value of another type **SHOULD** use the `into_` prefix. |
| [CR-NAM-10](comprehensive-rust-naming-conventions.md#cr-nam-10) | `to`: non-consuming conversion | A method that creates a new owned value without consuming `self`, and implies a type conversion, **SHOULD** use the `to_` prefix. |
| [CR-NAM-11](comprehensive-rust-naming-conventions.md#cr-nam-11) | `as_` and `_ref`: reference conversions | A method that returns a borrow of a type's primary piece of contained data **SHOULD** use the `as_` prefix; to distinguish two reference getters, use the `_ref` suffix. |
| [CR-NAM-12](comprehensive-rust-naming-conventions.md#cr-nam-12) | `by`: custom comparator or projection | A method that takes a custom comparison or projection function **SHOULD** use the `by` component (`_by`, `_by_key`). |

## [Google C++ Style Guide — Excerpts Cited by the Rust Guide](cpp-style-guide-excerpts.md)

| ID | Title | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [CPP-GOAL-01](cpp-style-guide-excerpts.md#cpp-goal-01) | Style rules should pull their weight | A style rule's benefit **MUST** be large enough to justify asking all engineers to remember it. |
| [CPP-GOAL-02](cpp-style-guide-excerpts.md#cpp-goal-02) | Optimize for the reader, not the writer | Code **SHOULD** be optimized for the experience of the average engineer reading, maintaining and debugging it, rather than for ease of writing it. |
| [CPP-GOAL-03](cpp-style-guide-excerpts.md#cpp-goal-03) | Be consistent with existing code | One style **SHOULD** be used consistently throughout the codebase. |
| [CPP-GOAL-04](cpp-style-guide-excerpts.md#cpp-goal-04) | Be consistent with the broader C++ community when appropriate | Standard features and widely known, accepted idioms **SHOULD** be used when they solve the problem, for the same reasons as internal consistency. |
| [CPP-GOAL-05](cpp-style-guide-excerpts.md#cpp-goal-05) | Avoid surprising or dangerous constructs | Constructs that are more surprising or dangerous than they appear **SHOULD** be avoided; restrictions exist to prevent these pitfalls. |
| [CPP-GOAL-06](cpp-style-guide-excerpts.md#cpp-goal-06) | Avoid constructs that the average programmer would find tricky or hard to maintain | Features whose complexity makes them not generally appropriate **SHOULD** be avoided. |
| [CPP-GOAL-07](cpp-style-guide-excerpts.md#cpp-goal-07) | Be mindful of our scale | Decisions **SHOULD** account for scale (100+ million lines, thousands of engineers), where one engineer's mistake or simplification can become costly for many. |
| [CPP-GOAL-08](cpp-style-guide-excerpts.md#cpp-goal-08) | Concede to optimization when necessary | Performance optimizations **MAY** be used when necessary and appropriate, even when they conflict with the other principles. |
| [CPP-GOAL-09](cpp-style-guide-excerpts.md#cpp-goal-09) | Common sense and good taste prevail | The guide aims for maximal guidance with reasonable restriction; common sense and good taste — meaning the established conventions of the entire Google C++ community, not personal or team preferences — **SHOULD** prevail. Clever or unusual constructs **SHOULD** be treated with skepticism and reluctance. |
| [CPP-NAM-01](cpp-style-guide-excerpts.md#cpp-nam-01) | Make the purpose understandable to a new reader | Names **SHOULD** make their purpose or intent understandable to a new reader, even someone on a different team than the owners. |
| [CPP-NAM-02](cpp-style-guide-excerpts.md#cpp-nam-02) | Scale descriptiveness with scope and context | A name **SHOULD** be descriptive even when used far from where it is made available, but **SHOULD NOT** distract the reader by repeating information present in the immediate context. |
| [CPP-NAM-03](cpp-style-guide-excerpts.md#cpp-nam-03) | Minimize unfamiliar abbreviations | Abbreviations likely unknown outside your project (especially acronyms and initialisms) **SHOULD** be minimized; you **MUST NOT** abbreviate by deleting letters within a word. |
| [CPP-NAM-04](cpp-style-guide-excerpts.md#cpp-nam-04) | Vocabulary names | If you define a new "vocabulary" name, you **SHOULD** get additional design review to make sure it works well when used widely. |
